Command: A priest shall not serve with long hair
Summary: The command: A priest shall not serve with long hair (Leviticus 10:6). In mourning for Nadab and Abihu, Aaron and his sons were not to let their hair go loose, a sign of mourning forbidden during service.
Commandment: A priest shall not serve with long hair.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches the earthly tabernacle was a copy of the heavenly one, and Christ now serves as high priest in the true tabernacle.
Purpose: To give Israel a mediated approach to God through the tabernacle pattern (Exodus 25:40). Hebrews teaches the earthly copy gave way to Christ's priesthood in the true tabernacle (Hebrews 8:1-6).
Function: In mourning for Nadab and Abihu, Aaron and his sons were not to let their hair go loose — a ceremonial law about the priest in grief. Its goal was to keep the priests in service even while the dead lay before them: the anointing oil was upon them, and mourning's signs were forbidden during the work. The evil was letting grief, even rightful grief, break the order of worship. It restrained that by holding the priests to their post, hair bound and garments whole, while they served.
